additional_questions_derived_not_shown.why: This record raised more judgement calls than a packet shows, so a reviewer is not handed a list long enough to skip. These are derived from the record's own fields and are recorded here rather than discarded, so nothing this tool found is lost. A reviewer who wants them should ask for them; the point of the cap is that the four highest-value questions are the ones that get answered.

links_touching_record.rationale: The use case is enabled by the item definition and its operational situations are drawn from the definition's situations; the link records that direction so the item's boundary is the reason the use case exists.

The system requirement refines the operational scenario's obligation into a measurable system-level statement. The use case is the parent and the requirement is the child, which is the direction refines runs in everywhere in this registry.

The measure validates the pack manufacturer's need and the charging use case against a full charge cycle, judging by delivered capacity and by the absence of a safe-state reaction. The relation is validates rather than verifies because the target is a stakeholder need or a use case, not a requirement: validation addresses intent and operational scenario, and the master prompt separates it from requirement verification for exactly that reason.

main_success_scenario.action: The charger requests a charge current flow
main_success_scenario.expected_observable_outcome: The item accepts and closes the contactors through the precharge sequence without any safety reaction

main_success_scenario.action: The charger ramps the pack toward its declared full state
main_success_scenario.expected_observable_outcome: The item monitors throughout and raises no entry that forces the safe state

main_success_scenario.action: The charger reaches the declared full state and stops requesting current
main_success_scenario.expected_observable_outcome: The item returns to a resting state with the contactors in their commanded position
At least 98% of the pack's declared usable capacity has been delivered

operational_scenarios.expected_item_behaviour: The item must not classify this as a violation and must not react, because the cell has not crossed the limit
operational_scenarios.expected_observable_outcome: No contactor opening and no fault indication; the charge continues to completion
initial_conditions: Cell-to-cell spread within the declared manufacturing spread
operational_scenarios.observable_by: The pack manufacturer, from the delivered energy and the item's own fault output
operational_scenarios.operational_situation: Vehicle parked, charger connected, pack charging at its limit
operational_scenarios.perturbation: One cell approaches the configured maximum limit and sits within the measurement noise band of it for longer than the debounce window
operational_scenarios.safe_state_interaction: Not reached. This scenario tests that the item stays out of the safe state when it should, which is the failure mode a one-directional validation would miss.

postconditions: The pack is at its declared full state and the item is at rest.
No diagnosis entry of a severity that would force the safe state is active.
preconditions: The pack is at or above its declared minimum state of charge.
The item is fitted and its configuration data matches the pack's build record.
A charger capable of the pack's declared charge rate is connected and respects the limits the item publishes (FB2-ASM-003).

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.
